html:
The Biri were an Aboriginal Australian people of north Queensland, in the Bowen River country inland from today's Bowen, a tributary of the Burdekin.

The name also covers a language. Linguists group the speech of several neighbours, such as the Gabalbara, Yambina, Yangga and Baradha, as dialects of one Biri language. On the coast lived the Giya. Cattle runs spread up the Bowen and Burdekin valleys in the early 1860s, soon after Bowen was founded.
sum: The Biri were an Aboriginal Australian people of north Queensland, in the Bowen River country inland from today's Bowen, a tributary of the Burdekin.
